thesis: Allah details His signs so the road of rebellion becomes recognisable, desire is refused the status of religion, and judgment is returned to Allah alone.

thesis: The storm is not scenery but theology: lightning trains the servant to hold fear and hope together, thunder and the angels are already in praise, and human disputation is the only dissonance in the scene.
notes: REPAIR CONFIRMED AND THE NEW WORDING MATCHES THE SOURCE SENTENCE ALMOST WORD FOR WORD. al-Tabari at 13:13, immediately under ‹ويسبح الرعد بحمده›, says: 'قال أبو جعفر: وقد بينا معنى الرعد فيما مضى، بما أغنى عن إعادته في هذا الموضع.' The new clause — 'he says he has already explained what *ar-raʿd* means earlier and sees no need to repeat it here, and refers the reader back to that place' — is a faithful rendering of exactly that sentence and nothing more. The retired clause ('which is where the disagreement is recorded') asserted the CONTENT of al-Tabari's earlier treatment, which lies outside the fetched range; the replacement asserts nothing about it. 'Does not settle the identification at this verse at all' also holds: al-Tabari defers the identification of *ar-raʿd* and then only glosses the tasbih neutrally ('ويعظم اللهَ الرعدُ ويمجِّده'), with الرعد as agent — which decides nothing between angel and sound. AL-JALALAYN ANGEL GLOSS RE-CHECKED AND EXACT: ‹ويُسَبِّح الرَّعْد› هُوَ مَلَك مُوَكَّل بِالسَّحابِ يَسُوقهُ مُتَلَبِّسًا ‹بِحَمْدِهِ› أيْ يَقُول سُبْحان اللَّه وبِحَمْدِه — the file's transliteration *huwa malakun muwakkalun bi's-saḥābi yasūquhu* and its report that *bi-ḥamdihi* is the angel saying *subḥān Allāh wa bi-ḥamdih* are both exact, and 'without hedging' is fair (Jalalayn states it flatly). The section's claim that the commentators disagree is real and is not a breadth overclaim: it names only the two editions it characterises and asserts nothing about the other two. For the record, the file's chosen reading (the sound) is itself carried by Ibn Kathir, who ties 13:13 to 17:44 and glosses the hadith of the speaking cloud as 'the cloud's voice is in reference to thunder'; al-Muyassar reads it as ar-ra'd's own tasbih 'indicating its submission to its Lord'. So the ikhtilaf is genuine on both sides and honestly presented, with the file explicitly marking its own reading as 'a choice among classical options rather than... the plain sense'. Whole-file rubric: verify_arabic 2/2, verify_morphology 19 verified / 0 failed. Countable claim checked: 'the line that gives the surah its name' — root رعد occurs in the entire Qur'an only at 2:19 and 13:13, so 13:13 is the sole occurrence in Surah 13. 'The classical explanations take this toward severe might, force, overpowering capacity' for *al-miḥāl* is grounded in al-Jalalayn (القُوَّة أوْ الأَخَذ) and al-Muyassar (شديد الحول والقوة والبطش), and the file already hedges 'even if translations vary at the edges'.
